title: Wobble and the Sparkly Pebbles
markdown:
Wobble the wombat lived in the snuggest, coziest burrow imaginable. Soft moss lined the walls. Damp earth always made him sleepy. He loved his burrow. It was the snuggliest, coziest home ever. But sometimes, when the wind whistled a whooshing tune through the roots above, his tummy did a funny little flip-flop. Not a hungry flip-flop. A wanting-something-more flip-flop.

His best friend, Iris the inchworm, wore tiny glasses. She loved drawing maps of new tunnels, little legs making neat wavy lines. Her home was a hollow in a gnarled root, always filled with the rustle of maps opening and rolling up.

One day Iris opened a super-duper old map, crumbly-crunchy like a biscuit left out too long, faded ink, edges that might flake away.

“Look, Wobble. A map of the Old Diggings. See this marked spot?” She pointed with a tiny antenna to a faded X. “They say it’s the Sunken Station. Full of the most beautiful shiny pebbles. Pebbles that sparkle like captured starlight.”

Wobble’s eyes widened. Shiny pebbles. He loved shiny things more than napping, and that was saying something. He pictured them filling his burrow, glinting like captured fireflies. Then his gaze fell on the winding dark lines of the tunnels. A tremor rippled through his whiskers. His paws felt cold and clammy, as if dipped in a puddle. Dark unknown places made his usually round tummy feel a little deflated.

A low rumble shook the earth, as if a giant were stomping underground. Bits of Iris’s precious map fluttered down like papery leaves.

“Oh dear, oh dear, oh me. This old map is falling apart. Cracking like a dry twig. If we don’t find the Sunken Station soon, the way might be lost forever. Then no one will ever see those sparkly pebbles again.”

Wobble looked at the crumbling map, then at Iris’s earnest worried face. He wanted the pebbles. More than that, he did not want Iris sad, or her amazing map lost to time.

“Don’t worry, Iris.” His voice came out a little squeaky, but he kept going. “We’ll dig. We’ll get there before the map is all gone.”

So, with a determined wriggle and a hopeful bounce, they set off, the last crumbly bits clutched in Iris’s tiny forelegs.

Dig, wriggle, bounce. Dig, wriggle, bounce.

Wobble’s sturdy claws scrabbled. Iris guided him with the nearly-in-pieces map, pointing with her antennae and humming a little digging tune so the dark would not feel so empty. Deeper they went, into tunnels that smelled of old roots, quiet earth, and a hint of something mysterious. Once they paused to let a rumble pass, ears flat, then wriggled on before the map could flake any smaller.

Sometimes they squeezed through tight spots, packed earth pressing close, Wobble’s breathing quick, fur too warm. Once a tangled mess of thick woody roots blocked the path. He pushed with his shoulder. Paws scraped rough unyielding wood. He imagined grasping bony fingers in the dark. A shiver ran to his tail. He wanted to curl into a furry ball and go back to the safe familiar burrow.

“I don’t think I can do this,” he whispered, voice swallowed by the quiet. He pictured inky blackness ahead, where he could not see his own paws. He tried a step. Paws felt stuck to the mossy floor.

Iris inched closer, nudging him gently. “Just one more push. We’re almost there. I can feel it in my antennae.”

With a final mighty heave his claws broke through into empty space. They tumbled, paws over nose, into a cavern so vast their little glow-worm lamps barely lit the edges. Cool damp air. Ancient rock. And there, piled high like tiny colourful mountains, were pebbles: smooth, round, glittering. Red like tiny fires, blue like sky, green like moss, some with purple and gold swirls. The Sunken Station.

But as Wobble turned, heart bursting, he heard a worrying crunch. The tunnel they had come through was collapsing. Dust billowed. The way back blocked.

“We have to go. Quickly.” Iris’s voice was tight with a new worry.

Wobble looked at the beautiful pebbles. His heart ached. He imagined filling pockets, burrow, every nook. The tunnel shrank. Earth groaned louder. A particularly perfect pile of sky-blue pebbles shimmered a little way off.

He hesitated. Paws twitched. He could almost feel their cool smooth surfaces. If I just grab a few more… Then a cascade of soil buried the path to the pebbles. That was the cost. He had to leave the find behind.

“Come on.” Iris was already inching toward a new narrow opening, a glint of hope in her tiny eyes. Wobble took a deep breath, turned his back on the shimmering hoard, and scurried after her.

They scrambled through the new passage, dusty and bumpy, small rocks tripping his feet, sloped thankfully upward. They emerged not far from the familiar roots of their neighbourhood, blinking in soft underground light. Wobble was tired, fur dusty, and safe. Iris, a little breathless, was already looking around with keen cartographer’s eyes. “We made it back.”

As they walked home a shadow flickered across the tunnel wall from a passing beetle. Wobble flinched, a ghost of the old fear. Then he stopped. He remembered the silent tunnel, the roots like fingers, and how he had kept digging when his paws were cold. He remembered the collapsing rumble and choosing to leave the treasures. The shadow was only a shadow.

He looked up at the roots. They still whistled when the wind blew. Instead of a flip-flop in his tummy he felt a quiet steady warmth, the sort that stays after a hard dig. He had gone into the dark and come back out, a little dusty, a little tired, and a whole lot braver.

Dig, wriggle, bounce — and home. That felt much shinier than any pebble.
